output.headline: Xi Jinping calls for extensive US-China cooperation and regular military dialogue at White House summit with Trump
output.standfirst:
Chinese president’s proposals to steer the superpowers away from military conflict include inviting 100,000 young Americans to China on student exchanges, amid intense AI and trade competition and analysts’ scepticism about longstanding stable arrangements

  • Trump-Xi summit – latest updates
output.bodyHtml:
Xi Jinping has called for extensive cooperation with Washington, setting out how the US and China can avoid the “Thucydides trap” that could put them on a military collision course amid rising tensions over artificial intelligence, trade and Taiwan.

The Chinese president laid out terms for a mutual understanding that he said could steer the two competing superpowers on to a road of mutual gain and away from future military conflict, at the start of his summit meeting with Donald Trump in the White House.

Xi said the goal should be conditions for “achieving the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and making America great again go hand in hand”, rather than confrontation, citing Trump’s political catchphrase.

“We should strengthen communication. China and the United States are different in national conditions, but through candid, in-depth and continued dialog, our two countries can understand each other better, seek common ground while shelving differences, and build up mutual trust,” said Xi, with Trump looking on.

“We should coexist in peace,” he said. “China and the United States, as two major countries, stand to gain from cooperation and will both lose in confrontation. Our two militaries should maintain regular dialog and improve mechanisms for crisis communication and prevention.”

With such conditions in place, Xi said, “the Thucydides trap can be overcome” – a reference to the phenomenon, defined by the Greek historian, of tensions that arise when an emerging power challenges the dominance of an established power.

Xi invoked the phrase in his meeting with Trump in Beijing in May, asking the US president how he planned to avoid it.

Xi’s proposals for lessening tensions also included the invitation of 100,000 young Americans to visit China on student exchanges. They come amid a period of intense competition between the two powers over artificial intelligence and trade, with each side imposing tariffs on the other.

Addressing Trump directly, Xi said: “During your visit to China this year, we agreed to build a constructive China-US relationship of strategic stability. I am ready to work with you to steer the giant ship of the China-US relationship on a steady course towards the future.”

Xi also extolled his personal relationship with his American counterpart, saying: “President Trump and I have respect for each other. We have built personal rapport and stayed in touch.”

Trump had earlier welcomed Xi and his wife, Peng Liyuan, to the White House, noting that he was the first Chinese leader to make a second state visit to the US. The previous visit took place in 2015, when Barack Obama was US president.

“President Xi and Madame Peng arrive at an important moment for America, the 250th anniversary of our founding,” he said.

Trump said that he had forged “a truly great friendship” with Xi. “President Xi and I have made tremendous strides on the issues facing our two countries,” he said. “Our teams have been working to encourage a more balances trading relationship, including the new market access for American farmers and ranchers.”

He said the current visit would include discussion over security, technology and AI – which he called “super intelligence”, a term he introduced in his speech to the United Nations general assembly on Tuesday.

The White House welcome ceremony followed Trump’s unusual step of going to Andrews air force base in Maryland the evening before to greet the Chinese leader and his wife on the tarmac.

Much of the same pageantry was repeated in Thursday’s ceremony, with both countries’ national anthems being played. Trump was flanked by his wife, Melania, while members of his cabinet and senior aides – including Natalie Harp, Trump’s dedicated assistant nicknamed “the human printer” by fellow staffers – looked on.

Trump and Xi were scheduled to hold bilateral talks after the ceremony and the welcoming speeches.

Both leaders adopted a harmonious tone, though analysts have voiced scepticism about the possibility of longstanding stable arrangements being arrived at over a host of issues.

A truce agreed between Trump and Xi in South Korea last year aimed at keeping tariffs lower, which had been due to expire in November, has now been extended until February, the US treasury secretary, Scott Bessent, said.

Analysts believe the extension suggests Trump continues to be dissatisfied with Xi’s concession offers on trade and wants to keep the pressure on in the hope of getting a better deal if the two meet again at the G20 summit scheduled to be held in Miami in December.

In the race for AI, the US has placed strict export controls on microchips, semiconductors, software and chipmaking equipment in a bid to slow China’s development.

Chinese imports have continued to surge into the US despite the trade war between the two countries. China is on course to run a $1tn trade deficit for the second year running.

• The headline and text of this article were amended on 24 September 2026 to correct a misspelling of Xi Jinping.
